h1:
Trang 4 Island Tour
Emerald Cave, Kradan, Cheuk, Ma
intro: The 4 island tour is the best-value way to see the Trang sea if it's your first time. One boat covers all the highlights: you swim through the dark tunnel into the Emerald Cave at Koh Mook, laze on the white sand at Koh Kradan, and snorkel the reefs at Koh Cheuk and Koh Ma — all in a single day, no overnight on the islands needed. We've put together the hour-by-hour program, big-boat and speedboat prices, hotel transfers, which pier you leave from, and the months when boats actually run. Checked for 2026.

blocks.html: What stands out about the Trang sea is that the islands are still quieter than Phuket and Krabi, the water is clear enough to see coral from the surface, and you can do it all as an easy day trip without sleeping on an island. The most popular tour is the 4 island package: the boat leaves the mainland in the morning, loops the Emerald Cave, Koh Kradan, Koh Cheuk and Koh Ma, then gets you back before evening. It's ideal if you only have a single day in Trang but still want to tick off all the sea highlights.

blocks.title: Check before you book
blocks.html: The fourth island on the tour isn't fixed. Some operators include Koh Ma, others swap in Koh Waen, Koh Ngai or Koh Ya depending on the swell and season. Before booking, ask exactly which island so it matches what you want to see, and confirm whether hotel transfers are included — plenty of operators charge for those separately.

blocks.text: The 4 islands, and what you'll find

blocks.html: Each of the four islands offers something different: Koh Mook is the hidden cave, Koh Kradan is the pretty beach, and Koh Cheuk and Koh Ma are the snorkeling spots. Listed in the order most boats stop at them.

items.name: Koh Mook — Emerald Cave
items.blurb: The highlight of the whole trip. You swim through a dark tunnel about 80 metres long to reach a hidden beach ringed by tall cliffs, open to the sky above, where the water glows emerald green — hence the name. You wear a life jacket and a guide leads you through holding a rope; it's easier to enter at low tide. There's almost nothing else like it anywhere.

items.name: Koh Kradan
items.blurb: A fine white-sand beach many call the prettiest in Trang, with clear water shading from green to blue that you can wade into the whole length of the beach. Shallow coral around the island makes for easy surface snorkeling. Most tours stop here for lunch and give you time to laze on the sand — it's where people take the most photos.

items.name: Koh Cheuk
items.blurb: The best snorkeling spot on the tour. The island itself is tiny and you can't land, but the water around it is full of colourful soft coral and schools of fish. It's fairly deep with a current, so the guide strings up a rope for you to hold. A good mid-route snorkel stop — weaker swimmers can just hold the rope and look down in comfort.

items.name: Koh Ma
items.blurb: A rocky island shaped a bit like a horse's head, with no beach to land on, but underwater there's boulder coral, soft coral, clusters of sea anemones and Nemo clownfish to see. It's the bonus snorkel stop before heading back to the mainland. Some tours swap this for Koh Waen or Koh Ngai depending on the swell, so confirm the name before booking.

blocks.text: What a one-day tour looks like

blocks.html: Big-boat and speedboat tours follow a similar program — the difference is that the big boat is slower but steadier and cheaper, while the speedboat is faster and buys you more time in the water at each stop. Here's the typical schedule for a big boat leaving from Pak Meng.

items.activity: Minivan picks you up from your hotel in Trang town or the Pak Meng side and takes you to the pier
items.note: Confirm the pickup time ahead. Most tours include hotel transfers, but some charge extra for them

items.activity: Meet at Pak Meng pier, collect snorkeling gear and life jackets, then board
items.note: Allow time for the guide's safety briefing

items.activity: Arrive at Koh Mook and swim through the tunnel into the Emerald Cave to reach the hidden beach
items.note: Wear a life jacket, a guide leads you through; the first stretch of tunnel is dark, so brace yourself a little

items.activity: Head to Koh Kradan to swim and take photos on the white-sand beach
items.note: The prettiest beach of the trip — leave time to relax on the sand

items.activity: Buffet lunch on Koh Kradan or on the boat, with time to refuel
items.note: The tour price includes lunch, drinking water and fruit

items.activity: Snorkel the soft coral and schools of fish at Koh Cheuk
items.note: The water is deep with a current — just hold the rope the guide strings up and look down

items.activity: Continue to snorkel at Koh Ma, looking for coral and Nemo clownfish
items.note: A rocky island you can't land on — it's underwater snorkeling only

items.activity: Head back, arrive at Pak Meng pier and take the van back to your hotel
items.note: Back in town by evening, you can go for dim sum or roast pork

blocks.title: Big boat or speedboat?
blocks.html: The big boat is comfortable, steady and cheaper, but takes longer to move between islands — good if you get seasick easily or you're travelling as a family. The speedboat is faster and gives you more time in the water at each stop, but it bounces more in rough swell and costs roughly 400–600 THB more. If you're short on time and want to tick everything off quickly, go with the speedboat.

blocks.text: How much does the 4 island tour cost?

blocks.html: Prices shift with the season, the boat type and the group size. These are the price ranges we actually saw from Trang operators in 2026 — use them to compare before booking, but confirm the exact figure with whoever you book through.

items: Big boat, Thai rate — around ฿800–1,000/person, including lunch, drinking water, fruit, snorkeling gear and a guide. The starting price many operators use is ฿850
Speedboat, Thai rate — around ฿1,200–1,500/person for adults; kids aged 4–11 are cheaper at around ฿1,200. Faster, with more time in the water
Foreigner rate — usually adds about ฿400/person on top of the Thai rate (national park fee)
Hotel transfer — some operators include it, others add around ฿200–300/person if you leave from Trang town
Private longtail charter — for a small group of 1–4, chartering the whole boat runs around ฿3,900–4,500/boat; more freedom to roam but no shared guide

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The prices posted online are usually the group-tour boat rate. If you turn up at the pier on the day, some operators won't take you or will charge more. Booking 1–2 days ahead is more reliable and usually gets you a better price. In high season the crowds build up and Koh Kradan and the Emerald Cave get packed — if you want to dodge the crowds, pick the operator with the earliest departure.

blocks.text: Which pier do you leave from, and how to get there

blocks.html: Most 4 island tours leave from one of two main piers, depending on which operator uses which one. Check with your tour which pier they use before you plan your own way there.

items.name: Pak Meng Pier (Sikao district)
items.blurb: The main pier most island tours use, right next to Pak Meng Beach with its view of the hill shaped like a reclining figure. It's about 40 km from Trang town, roughly an hour's drive, with parking and storage for around ฿100 a day. Most tours meet here around 09:00.

items.name: Khuan Tung Ku Pier (Kantang district)
items.blurb: Another pier some operators use, over on the Kantang side, about 45 km from Trang town via Highway 403, then 4008 and 4162. Some tours leave from here because it's closer to the southern island group. Check with whoever you book which pier they use.

blocks.title: If you're not driving yourself
blocks.html: A tour that includes hotel transfers is by far the easiest option — you don't have to find your own way to the pier, since Trang has no convenient public transport out there. If you book a tour without transfers, you'll need to rent a car or charter a van yourself, which is more hassle. We'd suggest picking a package that includes transfers from the start.

blocks.text: When to go, and when the boats don't run

blocks.html: The Trang sea has a closed season during the monsoon. If you're coming specifically for the islands, you need to pick the right window — otherwise you'll arrive to find the boats aren't running and waste the trip.

items: November–April — clear water, calm seas and the most reliable boat departures. This is Trang's high season and the best time for island tours
May–July — the rain starts but it's still doable, with moderate swell and tours still running. Prices are usually lower and it's less crowded

August–September — monsoon swell is strong, some islands close, and the Emerald Cave usually shuts around September. Boats may not run depending on the weather, so it's best avoided if you want the sea

blocks.title: Packing for the tour
blocks.html: Wear your swimsuit from the hotel, since changing rooms on the islands are limited. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, a UV shirt and a waterproof pouch for your phone. If you have your own snorkel mask it'll fit better than the shared ones, and bring some cash for drinks or souvenirs on the islands, where a few spots don't take transfers.

faq.q: Which islands are on the Trang 4 island tour?
faq.a: The core islands are Koh Mook (Emerald Cave), Koh Kradan and Koh Cheuk. The fourth island isn't fixed — some operators include Koh Ma, others swap in Koh Waen, Koh Ngai or Koh Ya depending on the season and swell. Before booking, ask exactly which island so it matches what you want to see.

faq.q: How much is the Trang 4 island tour?
faq.a: The Thai rate for a big boat is around 800–1,000 THB per person, starting at about 850 THB with many operators, including lunch, drinking water, fruit, snorkeling gear and a guide. A speedboat runs around 1,200–1,500 THB. Foreigners usually pay about 400 THB more, and some operators add 200–300 THB for hotel transfers.

faq.q: Which pier does the Trang island tour leave from?
faq.a: Most leave from Pak Meng pier in Sikao district, about 40 km from Trang town. Some leave from Khuan Tung Ku pier in Kantang district, about 45 km away. Check with whoever you book which pier they use — and a tour that includes hotel transfers is the most convenient.

faq.q: Which month should I do the Trang island tour?
faq.a: The window with clear water and reliable departures is November to April. Avoid the August-to-September monsoon when the swell is strong, some islands close, and the Emerald Cave usually shuts around September. May to July is still doable, with fewer crowds and usually lower prices.

faq.q: Can I do the 4 island tour if I'm not a strong swimmer?
faq.a: Yes. Every stop provides life jackets, and at the Emerald Cave a guide leads you through holding a rope. At snorkeling spots like Koh Cheuk and Koh Ma there's a rope strung up to hold so you can look at the coral without swimming yourself. Tell the guide ahead of time if you're not a strong swimmer and they'll keep a closer eye on you.
